subject: Acadia: combined GLBA / HIPAA / FERPA addenda — scope & next steps

From: Marco Rivera <mrivera@acadiacu.com>
To: priyom_das <priyom@redwoodinference.com>, laura_bennett <laura@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Acadia: combined GLBA / HIPAA / FERPA addenda — feasibility ask

Hi Priyom / Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We have an upcoming pilot (student-focused lending program) that touches both consumer financial data and occasional student health records provided by partner schools. Legal has asked I check feasibility of Redwood signing a combined set of regulatory addenda (GLBA + BAA + FERPA appendix) for the pilot. High level asks: 

- Can Redwood sign a single combined addendum (or a parent DPA + individual regulatory addenda) covering GLBA, HIPAA/BAA, and FERPA?
- Residency: we need US-only processing for a subset of data, and an audit trail of transfers.
- Subprocessors: full list and KMS/HSM details; ability to gate or exclude specific subprocessors for regulated data.
- Evidence: SOC 2 report, encryption attestations, sample DPA + BAA language redlines.
- Timeline: we are targeting a pilot kickoff in mid-August — what’s realistic?

I attached a short request brief with our expected data elements and retention windows. Can we set a 30-minute intake call this week to triage?

Attachments: Acadia_Addenda_Request_20270620.pdf (scope + sample clauses)

Thanks,
Marco Rivera
Lead Counsel, Acadia Credit Union
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marco Rivera <mrivera@acadiacu.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura@redwoodinference.com>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acadia: combined GLBA / HIPAA / FERPA addenda — feasibility ask

Marco — thanks for the clear brief and attachment. Appreciate the context.

Quick intake from our side: we can support combined/regulatory addenda in principle, but there are a few operational choices that materially affect feasibility, timeline, and cost. Proposed next steps:

1) 30-min intake meeting (we suggest Wed or Thu). I'll pull legal and privacy.
2) You confirm the canonical data element list (sample looks helpful — thanks). Specifically flag any PHI elements (e.g., treatment notes) vs. consumer financial identifiers.
3) We'll provide: current subprocessor list + high-level redlines for DPA/BAA/FERPA appendix, SOC 2 Type II (most recent), and a short mutual action plan (MAP) with estimated timelines for Dedicated vs Private deployment.

Operational notes for your team to consider before the call:
- If you require hard US-only residency with contractual subprocessor exclusions and HSM-backed keys, Private (VPC or on-prem) is typically required. Dedicated (Redwood-managed but reserved capacity) can often meet residency and SOC 2 requirements but offers less subprocessor exclusion flexibility.
- BAAs are scoped to PHI — we’ll need your confirmation on whether the school partners will be sending PHI and whether Redwood will be a business associate for that processing.

I’ll calendar a slot — do Wed 6/23 9:30am PT or Thu 6/24 11:00am PT work?

Best,
Priyom Das
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Acadia: combined GLBA / HIPAA / FERPA addenda — feasibility ask

Marco — looping in since this touches regulatory and product delivery. Short answers and clarifying asks: 

- Combined approach: we usually structure as a parent DPA + specific regulatory appendices (BAA, GLBA appendix, FERPA appendix). That keeps obligations scoped and makes redlines easier for legal teams. We can discuss signing a single multi-addendum agreement if that’s preferred by Acadia.
- BAA scope: BAAs are limited to PHI. Please list the specific PHI fields and the legal basis for Redwood being a business associate (i.e., will Acadia or school partners designate Redwood as a business associate?).
- GLBA: we need to confirm whether the data in question is customer financial information as defined under GLBA, and whether Acadia expects contract-level indemnities or a specific audit right cadence.
- FERPA: typically applies when schools are the data controllers. Where FERPA-covered data is routed to Redwood, we need explicit controller-to-processor language and scoping about covered records and retention.

Please see attached: redwood_regulatory_matrix_202706.pdf — it maps typical clauses + our recommended scoping language. Key ask for your team before the intake call: produce a short table (CSV or sheet) that maps sample data fields to regulatory regimes (PHI? GLBA? FERPA?) and desired retention. That will speed legal scoping.

On timelines: assuming the data map is provided within 5 business days, and no major policy exceptions are requested, we can deliver an initial MAP + redline within 7 business days, and a refined legal package within 2–3 weeks. If Private deployment is required, plan on additional lead time for infra (estimates below will come from ops).

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Hi Marco / team — operational follow-up from privacy/ops. A few practical notes and what we can provide quickly: 

1) Subprocessors: we maintain a live list (attached snapshot: subprocessors_202706.pdf). For regulated pilots, we can offer a tailored subprocessor gating process — i.e., we can exclude specific non-critical subprocessors for regulated data flows on a per-account basis, but exclusions that require re-architecting (e.g., replacing managed DBs or analytics vendors) may push timelines.

2) Key management: options: (a) Redwood-managed keys in HSM (FIPS 140-2) with KMS controls; (b) customer-managed keys in supported cloud KMS; (c) private deployment with customer HSM — each increases deployment timeline.

3) Residency / transfers: Dedicated deployments in specific US regions are supported; full on-prem Private installs are available for customers requiring contractual residency guarantees and subprocessor restrictions. For Dedicated we can provide contractual commitments plus routing limits; for strict residency + no-subprocessor exceptions Private is preferred.

4) Timeline (very high level):
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): MAP + initial redlines 7–10 business days; integration & SOC2 evidence review 2–4 weeks; pilot readiness 6–8 weeks.
- Private (VPC or on-prem): MAP + redlines 7–10 business days; infra provisioning & security onboarding 6–10 weeks; pilot readiness 10–14 weeks.

5) Cost signal: indicative service uplift for pilot-grade residency & gating typically falls into a premium band (ops + infra + legal onboarding). We’ll prepare a short cost bracket once we confirm the data map and required exclusions.

I’m attaching a snapshot of the subprocessors list and a short ops checklist. Also dropping a Drive link to our private deployment notes: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD_example_link

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Privacy & Compliance — Redwood Inference

Attachments: subprocessors_202706.pdf
